workflow: Automating WhatsApp message sending using the WhatsApp Business API requires manual session token refresh and re-authentication via QR code scanning when tokens expire.
trigger: Session token expiry after 24 hours or server restart
current_workaround: Developers write scripts to periodically re-scan QR codes from the WhatsApp Web interface, or use headless browser automation (e.g., Puppeteer) to manually refresh the session.
consequence: If session expires, automated messages stop; missed notifications or delayed responses can lead to customer dissatisfaction or SLA breaches.

workflow: Monitoring and sending alerts via WhatsApp requires manual intervention to maintain the WhatsApp Web session and handle occasional disconnections due to network changes or WhatsApp policy updates.
trigger: Server reboot, network change, or WhatsApp Web session timeout after 14 days of inactivity
current_workaround: Sysadmins rely on cron jobs that check session status and manually re-authenticate by scanning the QR code using a mobile device, often requiring physical access to the phone.
consequence: Alerting pipeline fails silently; critical operational alerts (e.g., server down) may not be delivered, leading to prolonged downtime.

target_role: Developer using WhatsApp Cloud API with Twilio or similar
workflow: Integrating WhatsApp Cloud API for bulk messaging requires manual handling of webhook verification, media uploads, and template approval, with no native retry mechanism for failed sends.
trigger: New message campaign or template submission
current_workaround: Developers build custom retry logic, manual webhook verification steps, and work with WhatsApp support to approve message templates, which can take days.
consequence: Delays in sending time-sensitive communications (e.g., appointment reminders) cause missed appointments and revenue loss.
